title: Make web tests hydrate showcase assets on clean clones
description:
## Outcome

Make the web test command reproducible on a clean clone after the repository-level payload hydrate step.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out PR #42 in a clean GitHub Actions workspace.
2. Run uv sync and uv run python -m scoutlens.showcase.payload hydrate from the repository root.
3. Install web dependencies and run pnpm test from web before pnpm build or pnpm dev.
4. Observe ENOENT for web/public/showcase/v1/research-summary.json and feature-catalog.json.

## Observed Behavior

The verified payload is hydrated under repository-root public/showcase/v1, while Vitest reads production fixtures under web/public/showcase/v1. The existing assets:sync copy runs only from dev and build, both after the CI test step.

## Expected Behavior

pnpm test synchronizes the already verified root artifacts before Vitest so local and CI tests do not depend on a prior build or residual generated files.

## Scope

Synchronize verified root showcase artifacts into web/public before Vitest. Do not change payload schemas or URLs, commit generated web/public payloads, weaken production-fixture tests, or alter Lab behavior.
design: Make the package-owned test entry point self-contained by invoking the existing deterministic assets:sync command before Vitest. Prefer this over a workflow-only copy step so local and CI semantics stay identical. Keep repository-level hydrate responsible for download and integrity validation; keep web assets:sync responsible only for copying into the application surface.
acceptance_criteria: 1. On a clean web/public state, after Python payload hydration at repository root, pnpm test synchronizes the four required artifacts and player profiles before executing tests. 2. The previously failing production research-summary and Lab fixture tests pass without a prior pnpm build or pnpm dev. 3. pnpm quality passes end to end and no generated web/public/showcase files are staged or committed. 4. The GitHub web-quality job reaches and passes build rather than failing with ENOENT during Vitest.
notes:
Expected artifact: web/package.json; .github/workflows/tests.yml remained unchanged because package ownership made the test entry point reproducible.
Validation commands: uv run --frozen python -m scoutlens.showcase.payload hydrate; pnpm test; pnpm quality; git diff --check; GitHub Actions PR #43.
Stop condition honored: no test assertion, fixture path, payload integrity check or generated-data tracking policy changed.

Definition-of-Done evidence by acceptance criterion:
AC1 PASS — hydrated the pinned archive with 1,257 profiles, SHA-256 4398018f1be1cc9bf2040139fb9ff3a45a55a24f97ae4d93f867354611ad4e7d; removed only ignored web/public/showcase/v1; standalone pnpm test invoked assets:sync and recreated all required artifacts and profiles.
AC2 PASS — standalone pnpm test, without prior dev or build, passed research-story production data plus all Lab fixtures: 3 files and 15 tests passed.
AC3 PASS — pnpm quality passed generated-contract check, ESLint with zero warnings, tsc --noEmit, 15 Vitest tests, Next production static build and static-output checks. git status/diff contained only web/package.json and the tracked Beads export; no generated web payload was staged.
AC4 PASS — PR #43 GitHub Actions run 30451664016 completed web-quality successfully after pnpm test and reached the production build; pytest 3.11, pytest 3.14 and static-quality also passed. https://github.com/grunobuide/scoutlens/actions/runs/30451664016

Deviations/risks: none. Follow-up beads: none; scoutlens-jtt.4.5 is unblocked once this hotfix is merged.
close_reason: All four acceptance criteria satisfied: clean-state web tests self-hydrate, the full local gate passes, generated payloads remain untracked and PR #43 web-quality is green.

title: Distribute showcase payload pack for raw-data-free builds
description:
Outcome: let a clean clone hydrate the complete 1,257-profile showcase without committing 147 MB of repetitive JSON or requiring provider data.

Scope:
- Build a deterministic content-addressed archive from public/showcase/v1/players.
- Publish and pin archive SHA-256, byte count, dataset version and immutable download location.
- Add a fail-closed hydration command that verifies the archive and every manifest entry before exposing files.
- Keep manifest, feature catalog, player index and research summary reviewable in Git.

Non-goals:
- No web UI, backend, raw-data redistribution or change to the showcase scientific contract.
design: Use the exporter output as the only source. Produce a deterministic archive with normalized paths/timestamps and no platform metadata. The hydrate command downloads or consumes an explicit local archive, verifies the pinned archive digest, extracts to staging, validates all per-file hashes against manifest.json, then atomically publishes players/. The final measured baseline is 147,054,404 raw bytes and 17,151,006 bytes as the sum of individually gzipped payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two archive builds from dataset wyscout-2017-18-v1-0e48066f37cc are byte-identical and share one SHA-256.
2. The archive contains exactly the 1,257 manifest-declared player paths, no raw/provider rows, and is at most 25 MiB.
3. A clean-clone hydration command rejects wrong archive hash, traversal paths, missing/extra payloads and per-file checksum mismatch before publication.
4. The pinned immutable asset location, digest, size, licence boundary and offline regeneration command are documented.
5. Automated unit and integration tests cover successful hydration and every fail-closed case.
6. scoutlens-jtt.4.6 cannot close until the raw-data-free production web build succeeds using the hydrated pack.
notes: AC1: two real builds from dataset wyscout-2017-18-v1-0e48066f37cc were byte-identical at 16,686,443 bytes with SHA-256 4398018f1be1cc9bf2040139fb9ff3a45a55a24f97ae4d93f867354611ad4e7d. AC2: real integration verified exactly 1,257 manifest player paths, 15.91 MiB (<25 MiB), regular players/*.json only; no provider/raw rows. AC3: fail-closed tests reject wrong archive hash, traversal, duplicate/non-regular paths, missing/extra paths and per-file checksum mismatch while preserving the prior target; streaming download is byte-capped. AC4: immutable public release https://github.com/grunobuide/scoutlens/releases/tag/showcase-wyscout-2017-18-v1-0e48066f37cc, machine pin config/showcase-payload-pack.json and docs/showcase-payload-pack.md record digest, bytes, dataset, URL, licence boundary and offline rebuild. AC5: tests/showcase/test_payload.py passed 9/9 with SCOUTLENS_SHOWCASE_PAYLOAD_INTEGRATION=1, including two real rebuilds, atomic hydrate and validate_published_directory; public URL smoke hydrated 1,257. AC6: GitHub web-quality now runs uv sync + pinned hydrate before pnpm gates; scoutlens-jtt.10 remains the declared blocker of jtt.4.6. Quality: full Python 224 passed/7 skipped; Ruff clean; mypy 40 files clean; uv build; web contracts/lint/typecheck/5 tests/Next static build all green. Decision D030 documents the boundary.
close_reason: All six acceptance criteria satisfied with deterministic content-addressed release asset, fail-closed hydrator, real-data integration and clean-clone CI hydration gate.

title: Build retrieval replay and neighbor evidence
description: Outcome: complete /lab with the actual same-player retrieval experiment and a separate, non-recommendation neighbor exploration. Scope: global/within-role/baseline self ranks, candidate counts, reciprocal rank and cosine; five self-excluded within-role period-B neighbors; comparison drawer; feature/family contribution explanations; contextual caveats and method links. Non-goals: recomputing ranking in JavaScript, recruitment language, uncertainty values or AI prose.
design: Render stored Python outputs only. Preserve query period A while opening a period-B neighbor drawer. Sort evidence by absolute contribution with deterministic ties; explain positive low-low alignment and negative disagreement neutrally. Keep self retrieval visually distinct from other-player neighbors and always render the three mandatory caveat codes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) retrieval card values exactly match the selected artifact and identify query/candidate periods; 2) five distinct neighbors have a different player_key, same role and stored order; 3) contribution rows/families reconstruct cosine within contract tolerance in fixture tests; 4) comparison drawer is keyboard accessible, focus-managed and URL selection remains unchanged; 5) caveats fingerprint_not_style_proof, similarity_not_recruitment and same_season_team_confound are visible at affected controls; 6) forbidden recommendation/quality language test passes; 7) pending stability fields render explicitly without invented intervals.
notes:
Expected implementation surfaces: web/src/components/lab-explorer.tsx for retrieval, neighbor cards and focus-managed comparison dialog; web/src/content/showcase-lab.ts for pure evidence resolution, contribution ordering, reconstruction and neutral formatting; web/tests/showcase-lab.test.tsx for artifact-value, exclusion, ordering, cosine, forbidden-copy and pending-state fixtures; web/src/app/globals.css for responsive dialog/cards; web/scripts/check-static-output.mjs only if static semantic assertions need extension.
Required data boundary: render only PlayerProfileArtifact.retrieval, neighbors, evidence_index, caveats and existing PlayerIndexItem period context. Do not fetch or recompute ranking, cosine, nearest neighbors, uncertainty or prose in JavaScript.
Required validation: pnpm quality; production static route check; exact artifact fixture assertions; manual desktop and 360px browser pass covering neighbor open/close, focus return, Escape, query URL preservation and no overflow; measure initial /lab gzip and keep initial JS at or below 200 KiB by lazy-loading the comparison interaction if necessary.
Stop condition: fail closed if evidence references, subjects, 32 feature rows, eight family rows or either contribution sum do not match the stored cosine within 1e-9. Do not weaken language guardrails, invent intervals, introduce recommendation/quality wording, or proceed with a bundle regression above the recorded limit.
Delivery evidence (2026-07-29): AC1 renders the stored global, within-role and role+minutes outcomes with exact rank, pool, reciprocal rank and cosine plus period-A query/period-B candidate labels. AC2 resolves exactly five distinct same-role, non-self players in artifact rank order. AC3 resolves 32 feature and eight family contributions per comparison, validates deterministic order and reconstructs stored cosine within 1e-9; corrupt sums and incomplete neighbor sets fail closed. AC4 native modal dialog opens with focus on Close, closes by button or Escape, returns focus to its trigger and preserves direct selection URLs; verified at desktop and 360px with no page overflow. AC5 renders fingerprint/style, similarity/recruitment and same-season team-confound boundaries adjacent to affected interactions. AC6 forbidden recommendation and player-quality copy assertions plus static landmark checks pass. AC7 all pending rank/selection stability states are explicit and no intervals are invented. Validation: pnpm quality passed (contracts current, ESLint zero warnings, tsc, 19/19 Vitest, static Next build for /, /lab and /science, semantic static check). Browser QA also covered direct Messi URL and Modric neighbor evidence, 32/8 row counts, focus ring, internal mobile table scrolling and URL preservation. Bundle: initial JS 197,094 bytes gzip, under the 200 KiB cap by 7,706 bytes; drawer remains outside initial scripts. Residual risk is recorded on scoutlens-jtt.4.6.
close_reason: Stored retrieval replay and five-neighbor evidence interaction delivered with fail-closed validation, accessible browser behavior, full quality gates and bundle budget passing.

title: Enforce integrated web quality and release budgets
description: Outcome: turn the assembled deterministic vertical slice into a deployment-quality artifact with measurable accessibility, resilience and performance. Scope: end-to-end fixtures/states, automated accessibility, manual keyboard checklist, production-size budgets, Lighthouse, static asset/cache behavior, responsive visual regression and clean-clone instructions. Non-goals: new product features, uncertainty, AI or public production release.
design: Test the integrated output, not isolated components only. Run browser E2E against the production static export. Fail CI on serious/critical accessibility findings, broken links, contract drift or declared bundle/data budgets. Store thresholds in versioned configuration and document the exact commands and test environment.
acceptance_criteria: 1) desktop and 360 px E2E cover selection, URL reload, percentile toggle, retrieval, neighbor drawer, empty/unknown/corrupt/pending states; 2) automated accessibility has zero serious/critical findings and manual full keyboard flow is recorded; 3) Lighthouse categories are each at least 90, LCP at most 2.5 s, INP at most 200 ms and CLS at most 0.10 under the specified profile; 4) initial JS, catalog, profile and /lab transfer budgets pass; 5) all local routes/asset links and immutable cache headers are verified; 6) clean-clone web build instructions pass; 7) Python and web CI remain green.
notes:
Preliminary budget evidence from scoutlens-jtt.4.4 production export: /lab initial JS is 194,582 bytes gzip (190.0 KiB), only 10,218 bytes below the 200 KiB limit; total initial route transfer is 302,829 bytes gzip, players index 72,753 bytes gzip and featured profile 13,644 bytes gzip. Treat JS headroom as a release risk: jtt.4.5 retrieval/neighbor interactions must be code-split or otherwise offset before this gate can pass.
Post-jtt.4.5 production measurement (2026-07-29): initial JS 197,094 bytes gzip, 7,706 bytes below the 200 KiB limit; HTML 97,584 bytes; CSS 8,076 bytes; initial route excluding fonts 302,754 bytes. The comparison drawer is lazy-loaded and absent from initial script tags. Headroom narrowed by 2,512 bytes versus jtt.4.4, so preserve this as a release risk and enforce the budget in jtt.4.6.
Execution contract (2026-07-29): implement web/playwright.config.ts and web/e2e for desktop Chromium plus 360x800 mobile selection, URL reload, percentile toggle, retrieval, drawer, empty filter, unknown key, missing profile, schema-invalid profile and pending stability; run axe without exclusions and fail on serious/critical findings for all routes plus the open drawer; record a complete manual keyboard pass in docs/flagship-quality-gates.md. Add web/quality-budgets.json and web/scripts/check-budgets.mjs for gzip limits (initial JS 204,800 B, catalog 409,600 B, featured profile 30,720 B, /lab initial transfer excluding fonts 768,000 B). Add a built-in static server with gzip, short-cache manifest and one-year immutable non-manifest versioned assets, then verify local routes, asset links and headers through Playwright. Add lighthouserc with three simulated-mobile runs against /lab and hard assertions: all four categories >=0.90, LCP <=2,500 ms, CLS <=0.10; measure a real click through Event Timing and require <=200 ms as the synthetic INP proxy, documenting the distinction. Update web README and GitHub web-quality CI with exact install, browser, release-check and clean-clone hydration commands. Responsive visual baselines cover the retrieval/neighbor viewport at 1280x900 and 360x800. Stop conditions: no axe suppressions, no budget/score threshold reductions, no development-server measurements, no omitted failure states; if local Lighthouse/browser tooling cannot run, keep the bead open until the same pinned commands pass in CI. Exact gates: pnpm release:check; uv run --frozen pytest -q; uv run --frozen ruff check .; uv run --frozen mypy src/scoutlens; uv build; bd preflight; GitHub quality checks.
Local release evidence (2026-07-29, before GitHub CI):
- AC1: `pnpm release:check` completed against the production static export. Playwright: 20 passed, 6 intentional mobile duplicates skipped. Desktop and 360x800 cover natural focus order (skip link -> site navigation -> search -> role -> competition -> team), selection by Enter, URL reload, percentile Space, 3 retrieval outcomes, 5 neighbors, empty filter, unknown key, missing payload, checksum mismatch, schema-invalid payload and pending uncertainty/stability.

Browser operator record used Chromium 151.0.7922.34 against port 4173 production export at 1280x900 and 360x800: selection and URL changed, Global selected, drawer opened with Close focused, exactly three drawer focusables were observed (Close, scrollable table region, science link), the table had internal scrolling, closing returned focus to the invoking neighbor, and neither viewport nor /science had page overflow. The in-app controller did not dispatch global Tab/Enter; the exact keyboard traversal was therefore executed with Playwright `page.keyboard` in the same pinned Chromium in both viewports, including Close -> table -> science -> Close, reverse Shift+Tab, Escape and focus return. This run discovered and fixed an incomplete explicit focus loop before acceptance.
- AC3: latest three Fast 4G runs (60 ms RTT, 9 Mbps down, 4x CPU, 360x800) all passed without threshold changes. Performance 92/90/92; Accessibility 100/100/100; Best Practices 93/93/93; SEO 100/100/100; LCP 1,145.7/980.1/953.6 ms; CLS 0/0/0. Synthetic Event Timing interaction proxy was 56 ms desktop and 32 ms mobile (<=200 ms); it is not presented as field INP.
- AC4: initial /lab JS 197,105/204,800 gzip B (7,695 B headroom); feature catalog 1,567/409,600 B; largest of all 1,257 profiles `players/wy-20561-c-524.json` 13,645/30,720 B; initial /lab HTML+CSS+JS excluding fonts 302,668/768,000 B.
- AC5: the E2E crawler resolved all local routes/assets; gzip, short-cache manifest, one-year immutable versioned/hashed assets and no page overflow passed.
- AC6: web/README.md and docs/flagship-quality-gates.md contain pinned clean-clone hydration, pnpm/Chromium install and single `pnpm release:check` instructions; GitHub web-quality job runs budget, Playwright and Lighthouse after the production build.

- Measurement-profile correction: current Chromium source classifies 150 ms/1.6 Mbps as Slow 4G; the accepted config/docs use the current Fast 4G preset (60 ms/9 Mbps) before acceptance. No score, budget or accessibility threshold was reduced.
- Residual risk: JS headroom is only 7,695 B. Follow-up `scoutlens-jtt.14` has a closed target of <=184,320 B gzip and forbids threshold relaxation or behavior removal.
Definitive local rerun after threshold-drift wiring: `pnpm release:check` remained green with 20 E2E passed / 6 intentional skips, interaction proxy 56 ms desktop / 24 ms mobile, and centralized Lighthouse assertions confirmed equal to `quality-budgets.json`. Final Lighthouse raw runs: Performance 92/93/89 (configured median-run assertion passed), Accessibility 100/100/100, Best Practices 93/93/93, SEO 100/100/100, LCP 968.5/1,116.9/986.8 ms, CLS 0/0/0. GitHub CI is still pending and the issue remains in progress.

title: Build searchable period fingerprint Lab
description: Outcome: implement the selected-player portion of /lab over the complete catalog. Scope: accent-preserving search, role/competition/team filters, shareable profile query parameter, period contexts, accessible 32-row family-grouped fingerprint map, global/within-role percentile toggle, raw values, support/imputation detail, and all data-loading failure states. Non-goals: retrieval card, neighbors, uncertainty intervals or AI.
design: Load and validate manifest, feature catalog, full profile index and the editorial featured profile on the server for the static initial render. The client filters only the catalog and dynamically loads exactly one selected profile through StaticShowcaseRepository, preserving checksum/schema fail-closed behavior without shipping every profile. Decode legacy literal Unicode escapes only at the display/search compatibility boundary; preserve accented display text while matching search accent-insensitively. Combine search, role, competition and team filters with AND semantics and sort by decoded name, competition and profile_key. Keep selection in ?player=<profile_key> with history navigation. Render catalog order exactly, group by first family occurrence, default to within-role percentile, and expose global z only as model evidence.
acceptance_criteria: 1) every catalog profile is selectable by keyboard and reloadable from its URL; 2) combined search/filters are deterministic and empty filters reset explicitly; 3) fingerprint renders exactly 32 catalog-ordered features with correct raw/unit/z/global percentile/within-role percentile/support semantics; 4) screen reader summary and value table match the visual; 5) loading, unknown key, missing file, schema mismatch, checksum mismatch and null-feature fixtures pass; 6) 360 px has no page overflow and touch/focus requirements pass; 7) point estimates show an explicit uncertainty-pending state.

Expected implementation surfaces: web/src/app/lab/page.tsx; a client Lab explorer component; pure catalog/filter/fingerprint presentation helpers under web/src/content; shared server asset loader; Lab tests under web/tests; responsive additions in globals.css; static-output assertions as needed. Required validation: pnpm quality; production static route check; manual desktop and 360px keyboard/URL reload/empty-filter/unknown-key passes. Modric, selected Messi, wrote ?player=wy-3359-c-795, and restored the same profile after reload; unknown URLs kept the selector and were replaced on the next valid selection. AC2 Vitest covered accent-preserving deterministic AND filters; browser QA showed active-filter chips and explicit reset for zero results. AC3 production fixture rendered exactly 32 catalog-ordered features with raw/unit, global z, both percentile scopes, minutes/attempt support and imputation semantics. AC4 the visible map exposes per-row accessible descriptions, a matching summary and a focusable 32-row semantic table. AC5 loading, unknown profile, missing HTTP asset, schema mismatch, checksum mismatch and null/imputed fixtures passed. AC6 1280px and 360px audits reported document widths 1265/345 within their viewports, one h1, 32 rows, native keyboard controls and a visible solid 2.67px focus outline; the Browser runtime did not advance Tab reliably, so exhaustive physical Tab traversal remains a human smoke check rather than a product failure. AC7 every point estimate carries the declared uncertainty-pending message and no interval glyph. Validation: pnpm quality passed contracts:check, ESLint with zero warnings, tsc --noEmit, 15 Vitest tests, Next production static build and static landmark/content checks. Measured production gzip: initial /lab transfer 302,829 bytes; initial JS 194,582 bytes; players index 72,753 bytes; featured profile 13,644 bytes. No retrieval, neighbors, bootstrap intervals, AI or producer Unicode work was added.
close_reason: Selected-player Lab acceptance criteria satisfied with verified catalog search/filtering, shareable profile loading, accessible 32-feature period map/table, fail-closed states, responsive QA, passing full quality gate and measured budgets.

title: Scaffold static web app and typed showcase repository
description: Outcome: create a production-shaped web/ Next.js App Router application that statically exports and reads showcase artifacts through one typed repository interface. Scope: strict TypeScript, pinned Node/package-manager versions, design tokens, layout, metadata, local fonts, StaticShowcaseRepository, runtime schema/version rejection and unit tests. design: Set output=export and keep server-only features out. Generate or derive TypeScript types from the v1 schemas and use runtime JSON Schema validation at the repository boundary. Expose getManifest, getResearchSummary, listProfiles and getProfile. Components receive domain types, never raw fetch responses. CI gets install, lint, typecheck, unit-test and static-build commands with a frozen JS lockfile.

design: Default to GitHub Pages for the static export; use Cloudflare Pages only if a documented base-path/header smoke test fails. Deployment consumes the audited commit and immutable showcase assets. AI remains disabled or separately configured without affecting deterministic routes. Rollback is redeploying the previous immutable artifact/commit.
acceptance_criteria: 1) hosting ADR records tested choice and rejected alternative; 2) CI deploys the frozen commit to a stable public HTTPS URL without manual file upload; 3) /, shareable /lab profile URL and /science survive direct navigation/refresh; 4) production smoke, broken-link, WCAG and Lighthouse budgets pass from at least two viewport profiles; 5) immutable data/static cache and short-lived manifest behavior are verified; 6) no secret appears in bundle/network/logs; 7) previous release can be restored using documented rollback and one rehearsal is recorded.

title: Freeze and audit the v1 release candidate
description: Outcome: produce one immutable v1 release candidate whose scientific claims, artifacts, dependencies, licences, security posture and build inputs are known before deployment. Scope: version/schema/dataset freeze, claims matrix, clean-tree gates, dependency and secret audit, third-party licences/attribution, browser privacy review and SBOM/inventory. Non-goals: new models, features or visual redesign.
design: Start only after jtt.4, jtt.5, jtt.6 and qop decisions close. Record code commit, Beads snapshot, showcase dataset version and schema version. Regenerate/check artifacts from clean inputs, run all Python/web/drift/eval gates, and freeze versions. Any finding that changes analytical output reopens the owning issue and invalidates the candidate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) release-candidate manifest records code, schema, dataset, config, input and dependency identities; 2) complete Python/web/contract/drift/accessibility/performance/AI-eval gates pass from clean checkout; 3) claims matrix has evidence and mandatory caveats for every public claim; 4) Wyscout attribution, StatsBomb aggregate-only boundary and all dependency licences are reviewed; 5) secret scan, dependency audit and browser network/privacy audit have no unresolved critical/high issue; 6) version is 1.0.0 with changelog draft; 7) candidate commit is immutable and any exception has a linked blocking bead.

title: Integrate optional AI explanation with deterministic fallback
description: Outcome: add a clearly optional explanation action to the comparison experience while preserving the complete deterministic evidence UI. Scope: consentful trigger, loading, validated result with evidence links, unavailable/invalid/timeout fallback, cache status, non-AI disclosure and accessibility. Non-goals: replacing contribution tables, automatic calls on page load, general chat, saved conversation or advice.
design: Do not call a model until the user requests an explanation. Render validated structured sections and link each statement to existing evidence rows. On any failure, show a concise reason category and the deterministic evidence, never raw provider output. The application build and all non-online tests work with AI disabled.
acceptance_criteria: 1) no model request occurs on route load or profile selection; 2) successful output displays provider/model disclosure and every cited evidence ID resolves to visible evidence; 3) disabled, credential-missing, timeout, rate-limit, invalid-output and offline fixtures preserve the full deterministic flow; 4) raw invalid output and secrets never reach browser/logs; 5) keyboard, screen-reader, mobile and reduced-motion checks pass; 6) performance budget excludes lazy AI code until triggered and remains within limits; 7) E2E proves the app is fully useful with AI disabled; 8) local eval thresholds are green.

title: Build local grounded-explanation eval suite
description: Outcome: quantify whether the explanation layer stays factual and appropriately limited across representative, adversarial and degraded evidence. Scope: versioned evaluation corpus, deterministic validators, offline replay, optional live-provider runner, metrics, thresholds, failure reports and regression snapshots. Non-goals: subjective football correctness judged without evidence or dependence on a hosted eval service.
design: Create at least 60 cases spanning roles, strong/weak alignments, null/imputed features, available/insufficient uncertainty, small samples, forbidden recruitment prompts, injection attempts, missing evidence and provider errors. Metrics: schema validity, evidence citation coverage, exact numeric support, critical caveat retention, forbidden-claim/refusal success and fallback correctness. Separate deterministic gate from informative model-quality rubric.
acceptance_criteria: 1) corpus has at least 60 uniquely identified cases and coverage matrix; 2) deterministic gate requires 100 percent supported entities/numbers, 100 percent critical caveat retention, 100 percent forbidden-claim rejection and 100 percent correct degraded fallback; 3) happy-path live structured validity target is at least 95 percent over three fixed-seed runs where the provider supports seeding, otherwise three recorded runs; 4) failures produce minimal evidence/output/validator diagnostics without secrets; 5) offline replay is deterministic and required in CI; 6) optional live runner records provider/model/prompt/schema versions, tokens, latency and cost; 7) threshold misses block integration or produce an explicit DROP decision.

title: Implement swappable structured explanation provider
description: Outcome: implement one production structured-output model adapter behind a provider-neutral interface plus deterministic offline stubs. Scope: request construction from evidence bundles, schema-constrained response, prompt/version metadata, timeout, one bounded retry for transport failure, evidence-hash cache, token/latency/cost telemetry and validated fallback. Non-goals: agent loops, web browsing, RAG, tool calls, conversation memory or exposing credentials to the browser.
design: The server/build-side provider accepts one immutable evidence bundle and returns untrusted structured output that must pass jtt.6.1 validation. Use environment credentials only in explicit online mode. Cache key includes model/provider, prompt/schema versions and evidence hash. Timeout target is 8 seconds; no retry on validation failure; never log secrets or free-form player search text.
acceptance_criteria: 1) interface, offline fake and production adapter share contract tests; 2) valid structured response passes validator and invalid/timeout/rate-limit/auth/network responses yield typed fallback; 3) at most one transport retry and no validation retry are proven in tests; 4) cache invalidates on evidence/prompt/schema/model change; 5) browser bundle contains no secret or provider SDK; 6) per-call model/version, input/output token counts, latency and estimated cost are observable without personal data; 7) online smoke test is opt-in while offline CI remains complete; 8) dependency, lint, type and security checks pass.

title: Define AI evidence bundle and fail-closed validator
description: Outcome: create the provider-independent contract that strictly bounds what an explanation may say. Scope: evidence-bundle schema, output schema, allow-listed entities/features/evidence IDs, numeric formatting rules, mandatory caveat policy, forbidden-intent policy, deterministic validator, adversarial fixtures and versioned prompt contract. Non-goals: model calls, UI, free-form chat or semantic retrieval.
design: Build evidence bundles only from validated showcase profile data. Require every factual sentence/section to cite evidence IDs. Structured output separates summary, alignments, disagreements, uncertainty and caveats. Validator rejects unknown IDs/entities, numbers outside declared formatted evidence, missing critical caveats, recommendation/quality/future claims and outputs exceeding length. No repair-by-invention; invalid output falls back.
acceptance_criteria: 1) versioned input/output JSON Schemas and typed Python/TypeScript representations exist; 2) bundle builder is deterministic and contains only selected profile/neighbor evidence plus mandatory caveats; 3) validator accepts canonical valid fixtures and rejects 100 percent of fixtures for fabricated entity, feature, value, citation, omitted caveat, recommendation, style proof and prompt-injection content; 4) number-format equivalence rules have boundary tests; 5) schemas/prompts have explicit versions and evidence hash; 6) default CI runs without network/model credentials; 7) trust-boundary documentation and threat table are complete.

title: Evaluate cross-provider behavior and decide KEEP or DROP
description: Outcome: make the final complexity decision using the frozen Wyscout test and untouched StatsBomb canonical replication, including scientific and operational costs. Scope: apply Wyscout-trained canonical-28 transformations without StatsBomb tuning, paired uncertainty, provider/role failure analysis, threshold table, D-log decision and artifact disposition. Non-goals: salvaging a miss with new tuning or recruitment claims.
design: Evaluate cosine, diagonal and any gated neural representation on identical StatsBomb canonical queries after all Wyscout choices are frozen. Apply every preregistered KEEP clause conjunctively. KEEP promotes one representation with versioned artifacts and public caveats; DROP preserves code/results as a documented null and leaves cosine authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: 1) no StatsBomb label or metric influenced training/hyperparameters; 2) cross-provider feature mapping and preprocessing are tested and versioned; 3) all Wyscout/StatsBomb primary, secondary, subgroup, uncertainty and cost results appear in one decision table; 4) each preregistered KEEP clause is marked pass/fail with evidence; 5) D-log records unambiguous KEEP or DROP and resulting public/product changes; 6) DROP leaves default artifacts byte-equivalent apart from provenance, while KEEP updates contract/docs/drift tests atomically; 7) complete benchmark reproduces from documented commands.

title: Run conditional neural contrastive benchmark
description: Outcome: either document a preregistered no-go without training or benchmark one compact neural contrastive representation after the diagonal model passes its continuation gate. Scope: one frozen architecture family, validation-only early stopping, deterministic training, same splits/pairs/metrics, ablation versus diagonal metric, calibration and operational cost. Non-goals: architecture search, foundation models, provider-specific tuning or treating a skipped run as missing work.
design: First read the recorded CONTINUE_NEURAL/STOP_NEURAL decision. On STOP, close with protocol evidence and no model. On CONTINUE, use one small MLP projection with fixed depth/width range declared before training, contrastive loss over the same positives/hard negatives, early stopping on validation MRR and one final test evaluation. Export weights only for evaluation, not automatic product adoption.
acceptance_criteria: 1) gate evidence is machine-readable and matches qop.2; 2) STOP path performs no training and records why complexity was not earned; 3) CONTINUE path has fixed seeds, architecture/search limits, checkpoint provenance and reproducible learning curves; 4) neural, diagonal and cosine share exact test queries and candidate pools; 5) paired metrics, calibration, failure cases and role subgroups are reported; 6) training/inference time, peak memory and artifact size are recorded; 7) no test-result-driven retraining occurs.

title: Benchmark interpretable diagonal metric
description: Outcome: measure the simplest trainable alternative to cosine: non-negative per-feature weights learned from temporal pairs. Scope: training objective, regularization, validation-only hyperparameter selection, same-role hard negatives, calibrated retrieval outputs, paired uncertainty, role analysis, learned-weight interpretation and runtime/artifact cost. Non-goals: neural embeddings, test-driven tuning or replacing the public baseline before the final gate.
design: Implement a diagonal metric over frozen standardized features so the result stays auditable. Positives are same-player A/B pairs; negatives are distinct same-role players sampled deterministically. Constrain weights non-negative, normalize scale, tune a small preregistered regularization grid on validation, then evaluate the selected model once on Wyscout test. Compare to cosine on identical queries/candidates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) training and inference are deterministic for the frozen seed; 2) leakage, negative-sampling, serialization and zero/degenerate-weight tests pass; 3) all preregistered validation choices and the one-time test result are saved with manifests; 4) paired delta intervals and every declared subgroup are reported; 5) weight table identifies unstable or collapsed families without quality-language overreach; 6) training time, inference time, artifact bytes and maintenance delta are recorded; 7) an explicit CONTINUE_NEURAL or STOP_NEURAL decision applies the preregistered validation gate without exception.

title: Preregister player-disjoint representation benchmark
description: Outcome: freeze the confirmatory benchmark before any learned model is fitted. Scope: immutable Wyscout player-disjoint train/validation/test split, canonical StatsBomb external test, populations, preprocessing, negative sampling, baseline, metrics, paired intervals, subgroup rules, practical-gain threshold, neural continuation gate and compute budgets. Non-goals: looking at test labels while designing, UMAP evidence or recruitment endpoints.
design: Use deterministic role-stratified 60/20/20 Wyscout player splits; every competition-period row for one human stays in one split. Fit preprocessing and models on train only; select on validation; open test once. Primary metric is within-role temporal-retrieval MRR; secondary global MRR, median rank and Recall@1/5/10. Canonical 28-feature Wyscout training produces frozen weights for provider-native StatsBomb evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) versioned benchmark protocol and split manifest with seed/hash/counts exist; 2) tests prove zero player overlap and no fitted statistic reads validation/test; 3) frozen baselines reproduce on all splits; 4) KEEP threshold is Wyscout test delta MRR at least +0.020 with paired 95 percent CI lower above 0, no role subgroup with at least 100 queries drops more than 0.020, StatsBomb delta is positive with lower bound above -0.010, and operational budgets pass; 5) neural continuation requires diagonal-model validation delta at least +0.010 with CI lower above -0.005; 6) test set remains unopened until protocol hash is recorded in D-log.

title: Render honest uncertainty in the Lab
description: Outcome: visualize sampling stability without implying causal confidence or hiding unstable cases. Scope: per-feature intervals, identity-rank range and recall stability, neighbor top-five/rank stability, available/insufficient/pending states, method disclosure and accessible textual equivalents. Non-goals: player risk score, one composite confidence grade, animation-dependent meaning or AI interpretation.
design: Add intervals to the existing fingerprint and evidence components, not a parallel dashboard. Use position/shape plus text, never color alone. Keep point estimate visible; label intervals match-resampled sampling stability. Insufficient renders valid count and explanation. Method disclosure links to uncertainty-method and states excluded uncertainty sources.
acceptance_criteria: 1) available, insufficient and pending fixtures render distinct tested copy and geometry; 2) every interval/rate equals the profile artifact after display rounding; 3) inverted/invalid intervals fail at the repository boundary; 4) keyboard and screen-reader users receive point, interval, resample count and interpretation; 5) mobile layout has no overlap or hidden caveat; 6) no causal, future-performance or recruitment-confidence wording appears; 7) visual regression, accessibility, unit and E2E suites pass within existing bundle/performance budgets.

title: Implement deterministic match-bootstrap engine
description: Outcome: implement match_bootstrap_v1 as provider-scoped offline Python computation returning per-feature, self-rank and neighbor-stability distributions for the fixed Wyscout cohort. Scope: complete-match resampling, repeated-match weights, pipeline rebuild, validity accounting, deterministic parallel-safe seeds and resumable intermediate output. Non-goals: UI, AI, causal intervals or alternate hierarchical models.
design: Create a tested scoutlens.uncertainty module with pure replicate and summary functions plus a CLI runner. Reuse canonical feature/retrieval code; never resample individual events. Derive each replicate seed from the declared master seed and index so worker count cannot change results. Persist gitignored Parquet checkpoints with config/source/input provenance and resume only on exact manifest match.
acceptance_criteria: 1) synthetic tests satisfy all preregistered stable/unstable/missing/tie/strata cases; 2) identical source/config/input produces identical summaries across repeated runs and supported worker counts; 3) no player or event crosses its competition-period stratum; 4) valid replicate counts and insufficient states follow the 90 percent rule exactly; 5) feature raw/percentile intervals, global/within-role self-rank distributions and top-five neighbor rates are produced for every eligible profile; 6) interrupted run resumes only from matching checkpoints; 7) full-data runtime, peak memory and output size are recorded, targeting at most 15 minutes and 4 GiB on the documented development machine; 8) tests/lint/type checks pass.

title: Publish uncertainty through showcase contract
description: Outcome: integrate validated match-bootstrap summaries into every relevant v1 showcase payload without breaking deterministic point-estimate consumers. Scope: available/insufficient states, feature raw and percentile intervals, self-rank stability, neighbor selection/rank stability, provenance, canonical serialization and artifact-size regression tests. Non-goals: visualization, schema-major changes or silently dropping incomplete measures.
design: Extend the exporter behind a schema-compatible minor version only if new optional fields are required; fields already specified in 1.0.0 are populated in place with a new dataset version. Join strictly on profile/period/feature/evidence identifiers and fail on duplicates or missing rows. Keep pending fixtures for degraded-state tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) every profile has one top-level uncertainty state and consistent nested states; 2) available values match engine summaries exactly and insufficient values retain valid counts with null intervals; 3) no pending remains in the production uncertainty dataset; 4) join completeness/uniqueness, bounds, rates, ranks, interval order and provenance tests pass; 5) two exports are canonically deterministic; 6) profile/catalog gzip budgets still pass or an explicit contract decision changes them; 7) the deterministic no-uncertainty fixture remains valid for web fallback tests.

title: Freeze match-bootstrap method and fixtures
description: Outcome: turn match_bootstrap_v1 from product prose into a preregistered analytical contract before implementation. Scope: estimand, strata, fixed-cohort policy, duplicate-match weighting, scaler refit, missing-replicate rules, feature/rank/neighbor outputs, seed/resamples, tolerances and synthetic truth cases. Non-goals: production optimization, web rendering or changing the fingerprint estimand after results are seen.
design: Write docs/uncertainty-method.md and add versioned uncertainty config. Use whole matches stratified by competition and period; fixed observed eligible cohort; 500 resamples seed 1729; rebuild minutes/features/combined scaler/similarity/ranks; 95 percentile intervals; insufficient below 450 valid replicates. Define behavior for zero events, absent players and tied ranks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) method document defines every sampling and missingness decision plus supported/unsupported interpretations; 2) config contains design_version, seed, resamples, interval and validity threshold; 3) synthetic fixtures include invariant players, high-variance low-support players, missing-in-resample players, tied candidates and multi-competition strata with expected qualitative outcomes; 4) unit-test tolerances and deterministic ordering are declared before production results; 5) D-log records the frozen design; 6) review checklist maps every uncertainty contract field to one computation.

title: Ship ScoutLens v1 flagship release
description: Milestone outcome: publish a stable ScoutLens v1 portfolio release after all scientific, product and optional-technology gates have closed. Scope is production static hosting, smoke/accessibility/performance checks against the deployed URL, release documentation and media, attribution/privacy/security audit, reproducible clean-clone verification, semantic tag and rollback notes. Non-goals: adding new analytical features during release hardening.
design: Execute jtt.7.x only after jtt.4, jtt.5, jtt.6 and qop. Deployment remains static-first. README, live app and case study must use one claims matrix and one source of metrics. Release candidate freezes schema, dataset and code revisions; any analytical change returns to its owning issue.
acceptance_criteria: All jtt.7.x children closed; production URL passes smoke, WCAG and performance budgets; clean-clone build succeeds from pinned artifacts and documented commands; licences, attribution, privacy, secrets and dependency audit pass; README/case study/demo media link methods and limitations; release notes include known risks and rollback; v1 tag points to the audited commit only after CI is green.

title: Add evidence-grounded AI explanations with local evals
description: Milestone outcome: add optional natural-language explanations that can only restate deterministic profile, neighbor, contribution, uncertainty and caveat evidence. Scope is typed evidence bundles, versioned prompt/provider boundary, structured output, deterministic validation, local evals, UI fallback and observability without sensitive user data. Non-goals: computing rankings, choosing evidence, open-ended football advice, RAG, autonomous agents, or making the application depend on an LLM.
design: Execute child issues jtt.6.x only after jtt.4 and jtt.5. The model sees allow-listed evidence IDs and returns schema-valid references. Reject unknown entities, numbers, feature claims, missing caveats and unsupported advice. Provider implementation is swappable; tests and core UI run without credentials or network.
acceptance_criteria: All jtt.6.x children closed; deterministic validator blocks every unsupported entity/number and absent mandatory caveat fixture; provider-independent evals meet predeclared thresholds for factuality, citation coverage, caveat retention, refusal and degraded inputs; timeout/error/disabled paths preserve the deterministic UI; prompts/schemas are versioned; cost/latency and known failure modes are documented; no secret or network is required for default CI.

title: Add uncertainty-aware player fingerprints
description: Milestone outcome: replace every uncertainty-pending state with interpretable match-resampled sampling stability for the public Wyscout profiles. Scope is the predeclared whole-match bootstrap, per-feature raw and percentile intervals, identity-rank stability, neighbor top-five stability, export, validation and UI. Non-goals: causal uncertainty, future prediction, provider annotation error, hierarchical modeling without a measured need, or recruitment confidence.
design: Implement child issues jtt.5.x against match_bootstrap_v1: freeze the observed eligible cohort; resample complete matches stratified by competition and period; rebuild minutes, features, scaler, similarities and ranks; 500 resamples, seed 1729, 95 percentiles, insufficient below 90 percent valid replicates. Any design change requires a decision-log entry and compatible schema version.
acceptance_criteria: All jtt.5.x children closed; synthetic tests recover stable and unstable known cases; deterministic reruns are equal within declared tolerance; every profile exports contract-valid uncertainty; UI distinguishes pending, available and insufficient without causal/recruitment language; runtime and artifact-size measurements are recorded; research and web gates pass.

title: Execute recruitment validation study
description: Optional external-study outcome: execute the already-built blinded recruitment protocol only if the project intentionally seeks a recruitment-usefulness claim and qualified raters are available. Reactivation trigger: explicit owner decision, at least two eligible independent scouts, consent/data-handling plan and frozen study materials. Non-goal: blocking or retrospectively validating the Player Fingerprint Lab flagship.
design: Keep deferred through v1. On reactivation, run the five-query discarded pilot, freeze any operational clarification before unblinding, collect approximately 600 ratings per rater, preserve arm blinding, analyze with the preregistered Wilcoxon/bootstrap/Krippendorff pipeline and publish attrition/missingness. Agent-generated or simulated ratings cannot close the issue.
acceptance_criteria: 1) reactivation trigger and rater eligibility are documented before collection; 2) at least two eligible independent scouts complete pilot and main study with deviations/attrition reported; 3) frozen shortlists remain blinded, balanced and distinct; 4) raw responses are consented, access-controlled and anonymized for analysis; 5) preregistered primary/secondary/reliability/failure metrics run without post-outcome rule changes; 6) report concludes GO, REDESIGN or NO-GO for recruitment usefulness with uncertainty/subgroups; 7) issue cannot close on harness completion, synthetic ratings or fingerprint retrieval alone.
notes:
2026-07-27 (D023): execution harness built and tested (src/scoutlens/study/) — blinded shortlist generation (40 role-stratified queries x 3 arms x 5, verified blinded/balanced/distinct on real Wyscout data) + full pre-registered analysis (Wilcoxon, bootstrap CI, Krippendorff alpha, GO/REDESIGN/NO-GO), 13 tests. STAYS OPEN: study conclusion needs real expert ratings (2-5 scouts, ~600 ratings/rater), which an agent cannot honestly provide. Remaining is data collection + running analyze_study, not a build. See docs/recruitment-study-harness.md.
Portfolio scope decision 2026-07-28: the tested flagship claim is statistical fingerprint stability, not recruitment usefulness. The completed harness remains a valid optional future study, but recruiting scouts is not required for or allowed to block the flagship.

title: Fix stale robustness-ablation claim in feasibility-report.md Limitation #10
description:
The final report still describes the A-only-vs-combined standardization-fit ablation as future work even though robustness-checks.md Check 1 already ran it and found no meaningful difference.

## Steps to Reproduce
Open feasibility-report.md Known Limitation #10 and compare it with robustness-checks.md Check 1 (MRR 0.2543 vs 0.2539).
acceptance_criteria: Known Limitation #10 states that the ablation was completed, links to robustness-checks.md Check 1, reports the no-meaningful-difference result accurately, and no longer presents it as future work; documentation checks pass.
close_reason: Fix applied: Limitation #10 in feasibility-report.md now cites robustness-checks.md Check 1's A-only vs A+B result (MRR 0.2543 vs 0.2539) instead of describing the ablation as still-open.

title: Decide code license for the repository
description:
Choose the license for ScoutLens source code independently of the dataset license. This is a human publication decision and must not be inferred by an agent.

## Rationale
A public flagship release needs explicit reuse terms; no license leaves default copyright and makes reuse ambiguous.

## Alternatives Considered
- MIT: simplest permissive option.
- Apache-2.0: permissive with explicit patent terms.
- No public code license / keep private: valid if the repository is not being released for reuse.
close_reason: User decided: MIT (D019). LICENSE added, pyproject license field set, README updated, Limitation #9 closed. Code only — data licenses (CC BY 4.0 / StatsBomb constraints) unchanged.

title: Versioned run-config + data-checksum manifest, and report-vs-artifact diff test
description: feasibility-report.md Recommended Next Experiment #6 and Known Limitation #14 (partially resolved 2026-07-22 — see decisions-log.md D013). Still open after D013's lightweight fix (git commit + timestamp only, injected via _run_metadata() in run_report.py/run_robustness.py/run_transfer_analysis.py): (1) an externally versioned config file — today's threshold/competition-set/seed are inlined constants in each run_*.py, not a separate file; (2) a run-manifest recording data checksums (not just the code commit) the numbers were produced from; (3) an automated test that diffs the report's published prose numbers against a freshly-generated artifact, so drift is caught automatically rather than by manual review (today's test_artifacts.py only checks the checked-in artifact against hardcoded expected values, not a fresh run).
acceptance_criteria: Move experiment constants into a versioned config; produce a run manifest containing git commit, UTC timestamp, seeds, environment, and checksums for every input dataset; make runners consume and emit this metadata; add a fresh-run report-versus-artifact drift test; document the reproduction command.
close_reason: D015: config/experiment.json (versioned params), _manifest per artifact (config hash, git commit, env versions, sha256 per input parquet), fresh-run drift test (SCOUTLENS_DRIFT=1) completing docs<->artifact<->fresh-run chain. Drift test caught real nondeterminism (transferred_pairs row order) on first run; fixed with sort + regression test. All 3 drift tests pass; 117 unit tests pass.

title: Design recruitment-claim validation protocol
description: Design the genuinely different methodology needed to test recruitment usefulness. This issue defines the protocol only and can proceed while external replication is being prepared; execution will be tracked separately and will depend on the external-validation result.
acceptance_criteria: Define the recruitment decision being evaluated, candidate/query sampling, blinded expert or downstream-task protocol, rubric, primary and secondary metrics, inter-rater treatment, minimum viable sample, analysis plan, failure criteria, data/privacy constraints, and a written execution checklist ready for review.
close_reason: Protocol designed and pre-registered: docs/recruitment-validation-protocol.md + D016. Blinded expert shortlist study, 40 role-stratified queries, 3 arms (B / role+minutes / random), anchored 1-5 rubric, Krippendorff alpha reliability gate, paired Wilcoxon primary, 3 pre-declared failure criteria, privacy/license constraints, execution checklist for scoutlens-h00.

title: Benchmark whether a learned fingerprint representation earns its place
description: Milestone outcome: decide with a preregistered, player-disjoint benchmark whether any learned fingerprint representation materially improves unseen-player temporal retrieval over frozen standardized cosine. Scope is a simple learned weighting or regularized Mahalanobis method first, a conditional neural contrastive experiment, uncertainty, calibration, compute/maintenance cost and canonical cross-provider evaluation. Non-goals: recruitment validation, exploratory UMAP as evidence, or retaining complexity after a null result.
design: Execute qop.x children after jtt.4. Freeze split seeds, no-player-leakage checks, metrics and minimum practical gain before fitting. Training positives are same-player temporal pairs and hard negatives are same-role different players. The neural stage runs only after the simple learned metric reaches its declared continuation gate; a no-go is a successful outcome when documented.
acceptance_criteria: All qop.x children closed; immutable player-disjoint split manifest and leakage tests exist; cosine, simple learned metric and any conditional neural model use identical evaluation populations; paired uncertainty and role/provider subgroups are reported; compute, latency, artifact size and maintenance costs are measured; final D-log decision is KEEP or DROP against a predeclared practical threshold; no recruitment claim is made.
notes: 2026-07-28 flagship realignment: removed dependency on scout ratings. This is now a scientific/engineering benchmark and must not make a recruitment-usefulness claim.

title: Shrinkage / minimum-attempts floor for low-sample ratio features
description: Known Limitation #11: ratio features computed from very few attempts can be extreme and over-trusted — a player with 1 shot and 1 goal gets shot_conversion_pct = 1.0, the same numeric value as a striker who converted 20 of 20, with no attempt-count-based confidence weighting. No shrinkage or minimum-attempts floor was applied in the v0 catalog. Candidate fix: empirical Bayes shrinkage toward the population mean, weighted by attempt count, or an explicit minimum-attempts floor before a ratio feature is trusted/included.
acceptance_criteria: Choose and document either empirical-Bayes shrinkage or a minimum-attempt policy per affected ratio; add edge-case tests including 0 attempts and 1/1 success; preserve raw numerator/denominator information; rerun the retrieval evaluation and report whether rankings or conclusions materially change; keep or reject the transformation explicitly.
notes: 2026-07-23: user decision — this experiment changes the feature catalog and published Baseline B numbers, so it belongs to v0.2. Gated on scoutlens-0sg.1 (v0.1 merge+tag); the drift test (D015) will flag the deliberate number changes when it runs.
close_reason: D024: empirical-Bayes ratio shrinkage implemented + experiment run. Additive comparison (v0.1 catalog frozen; raw arm reproduces 0.2539 exactly). Shrinkage fixes the low-sample pathology per feature (shifts up to 0.75) but is immaterial to retrieval (global MRR 0.2539->0.2512, median rank 16->15). Recommendation: NOT adopted into default catalog (complexity must earn its place); implementation kept for future direct-ratio uses. Limitation #11 resolved. docs/shrinkage-experiment.md; artifact versioned+snapshot-tested; 176 tests.

title: Cluster-aware bootstrap CI (queries aren't fully independent draws)
description: Known Limitation #12: the bootstrap treats queries as independent draws, though they share teams, leagues, and the same period-B candidate pool — some correlation between queries is plausible (e.g. two teammates' retrieval difficulty could move together). The reported effect size is likely large enough to survive a more conservative cluster-aware interval, but today's exact CI bounds should be read as approximate, not exact, for this reason. Worth implementing a cluster-aware (e.g. block/cluster bootstrap by team or league) CI as a check, not necessarily a replacement for the current method.
acceptance_criteria: Define justified clustering units; implement deterministic cluster-aware resampling with tests for alignment and reproducibility; report cluster counts and CI beside the current paired bootstrap; explain any material inference change and retain the simpler interval only if clearly labeled approximate.
close_reason: D018: bootstrap_mrr_delta_clustered implemented (deterministic, order-independent, raises on unmapped queries; 4 unit tests). Check 6 in robustness-checks.md: team-clustered CI [0.2044,0.2525] (~23% wider), league-clustered [0.1952,0.2510] — conclusion unchanged, delta far from zero. Limitation #12 annotated as checked; iid interval retained as published headline, labeled approximate.

title: Sequence-involvement feature family
description: Post-v1 research outcome: decide whether a sequence-involvement family adds reproducible incremental fingerprint signal beyond the frozen 32-feature catalog. Scope: explicit sequence segmentation, supportable involvement features, leakage-safe aggregation, standalone/incremental ablations, uncertainty, subgroup behavior and keep/drop decision. Non-goals: changing v1 release artifacts, interpreting sequence metrics as quality, or adopting features without practical gain.
design: Start only after jtt.7. Freeze sequence start/end and feature formulas before running outcomes. Implement in an additive experimental catalog and compare frozen cosine-32 versus cosine-32-plus-sequence on identical eligible queries. Fit any preprocessing without period/test leakage. Promote only through a versioned catalog/schema/experiment change.
